$comment: Every UI surface a config/integration-manifest.json entry may name, and whether it exists. `built` is mechanical: tools/integration-audit/verify-parity.mjs requires the named component to exist and to render data-surface="<surfaceId>". The manifest's per-entry `reachable` is the claim that a user can actually configure that integration through the surface, and it may only be true where the surface is built. The two are separate because a surface can exist and still not configure everything it lists -- see Settings > Transcription below.

Settings > Providers.note: Stores a key for every one of the fifteen credential slots the registry declares, and runs the real connection test. Write-only: no command returns a credential value, so the field replaces or removes and never displays. A stored key is reported as stored, never as connected.

Settings > Transcription.note: Chooses the cloud provider and model for dictation, from the registry. Six of the seven providers can be selected: three over HttpBatch and three through their own client in crates/transcription-core/src/clients.rs. Corti also takes an environment and a tenant here, because the router refuses to guess either. Tinfoil is listed with the reason it is refused -- an unattested request would present as Tinfoil while providing none of what the name means. Keys are stored on Settings > Providers.

Settings > Transcription > Local.note: Offers whisper models only. Parakeet and Nemotron need the sherpa-onnx sidecar, which does not exist, so those four entries stay unreachable while the surface itself is built.

Settings > Intelligence.note: Configures the reasoning provider and model that tidy a dictation, and switches cleanup on. The three enterprise connectors and the local route are listed with the reason they cannot be used, rather than being left out -- so this surface is built while Settings > Intelligence > Enterprise and > Local are not.

Settings > Intelligence > Local.note: Installs and runs the pinned llama.cpp CPU build and any of the registry's GGUF models. Sizes are shown before the install button because the recommended model is 5.9 GB, and the five-minute idle shutdown is stated rather than being a surprise later.

Settings > Intelligence > Enterprise.note: A form per connector on the Intelligence screen. The request signing and body shapes are written and tested against AWS's published SigV4 vectors and recorded fixtures; no live call has been made, and the section says so on screen as well as in PLATFORM_SUPPORT.md.

Settings > Meetings.note: crates/meeting-core holds the trait and the capability model and none of the five WebSocket clients.

Integrations > CLI.note: The CLI is complete and tested against the running API as a compiled binary, but nothing in the application tells a user it exists or where the discovery file is.

Notes > Upload.note: Phase 8. Audio, video and URL import need the ffmpeg and yt-dlp sidecars, neither of which is in config/sidecars.json.
